source.title: Epoch Capabilities Index: ECI model scores (eci_scores.csv, updated 19 Nov 2026)

scale: Epoch's current ECI scale (Bayesian method since 4 Nov 2026). Anchors: Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130, GPT-5 = 150.

reasoning.fit: Epoch's reasoning frontier from o1-mini (12 Sep 2024); end of window not stated (Epoch's brief calls it the pre-Astra trend)

previous.note: Epoch's 1 Sep 2026 fit on the old method (o1-mini to Claude Fable 5). Not on the scale of the points above.

from.note: Top of the models in Epoch's 1 Sep table, re-scored on the current scale. That table, on the old scale, showed Claude Fable 5 on top at 162.48.

to.note: GPT-6.2 Astra 174.17 (17 Nov); Claude Fable 5.2 173.5 (9 Nov, preliminary). Their 90% intervals overlap almost entirely.

latest.arithmetic: Our arithmetic: +9.43 points in 11 weeks (77 days). At 16.6 a year that is about 7 months of trend, 2.7 times the trend pace. Counting Claude Fable 5.1 (167.09, released 1 Sep) as the start instead: +7.08, about 5 months.

caveats: Every point comes from one file on one scale: Epoch's eci_scores.csv, updated 19 Nov 2026 (Bayesian method since 4 Nov).
Dates are Epoch's release dates. A model is listed when its ECI beat every model dated before it in that file.
Epoch's data starts 24 Feb 2023 (LLaMA-65B, 101.38), which was not the frontier. Like Epoch's own trend analysis, the series starts at GPT-4.
Left out: GPT-4 Turbo (Nov 2023), 124.75. Epoch dates it 25 Jan 2024 but its name says Nov 2023. On either date it falls between GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus.
GPT-5.3 Codex was a frontier point in Epoch's 1 Sep table (156.22, old scale) but is not in the 19 Nov file, so it is not shown.
On the new scale Claude Opus 5 (164.74) edges Claude Fable 5 (164.21); on the old scale it was below. Steps this small sit well inside the 90% intervals (about ±2 to ±4 points).
Claude 3.5 Sonnet (130) and GPT-5 (150) fix the scale, so they have no interval.
Claude Fable 5.2's score is preliminary. Epoch (9 Nov): based on pre-launch testing using only its own benchmarks, and may change.
Don't mix scales: 162.48 (old method, 1 Sep) against 174 (new method) overstates the climb. On one scale it is 164.74 to 174.17.
